standard: Zeek TSV logs (conn, dns, ssl, http, files, x509, notice); CSV exports from a SIEM, a remote-access gateway, a historian, a change system, mail gateways and a web portal
clock: All times UTC. Epoch seconds in Zeek logs count from 1970 (2027-09-14T00:00:00Z is 1820880000). Records in different systems that describe the same action agree to within a few seconds; log evidence of a session or write precedes its effect.
sampling: Network sensor: user-driven traffic and internal service chatter are a 1-in-200 sample. Recorded in full: periodic machine-to-internet traffic (endpoint agents, licence, update and feed checks, external time synchronisation), the mail transfers of every message in the mail gateway log, remote-access gateway and VPN sessions, and the flows behind alerts and audit records. Mail gateway: a sample of ordinary mail plus every message behind a mail alert. Audit tables and SIEM alerts: complete.

files.network_logs/zeek/YYYY-MM-DD/ssl.log: ts, uid, id.*, version, cipher, server_name, resumed, established, cert_chain_fps
files.network_logs/zeek/YYYY-MM-DD/http.log: standard Zeek http fields (plain HTTP only)
files.network_logs/zeek/YYYY-MM-DD/files.log: standard Zeek files fields (files seen in plain HTTP: sizes and hashes, no content)
files.network_logs/zeek/YYYY-MM-DD/x509.log: standard Zeek x509 fields (certificates seen in TLS 1.2 handshakes)
files.network_logs/audit/mail_url_clicks_*.csv: time_utc, gateway, mailbox, url_host, client_ip (+ message_id, sender_network for the vendor gateway); one row for every link in delivered mail that a recipient followed in the window; client_ip is an inside address for links followed at a workstation and an outside address for links followed on a phone or at home

ids: Host names, addresses, users and equipment come from gw_host_registry.json; account_ref in the aid portal log is the account_id of payments/aid_applications.csv.

column_notes.scada_command_log.origin: how the command reached the SCADA server: console, remote desktop, or automation
column_notes.scada_command_log.console_session_id: console logon session when origin is console
column_notes.scada_command_log.origin_host: host a remote desktop session came from
column_notes.zeek conn.log: ts, uid, id.orig_h, id.orig_p, id.resp_h, id.resp_p, proto, service, duration, orig_bytes, resp_bytes, conn_state, local_orig, local_resp, missed_bytes, history, orig_pkts, orig_ip_bytes, resp_pkts, resp_ip_bytes (standard Zeek meanings; conn_state SF/S0/REJ/RSTO/RSTR/SH/OTH)
column_notes.zeek dns.log: ts, uid, id.orig_h, id.orig_p, id.resp_h, id.resp_p, proto, trans_id, query, qclass_name, qtype_name, rcode_name, AA, RD, RA, answers, TTLs; uid equals the uid of the UDP/53 row in conn.log
column_notes.zeek ssl.log: ts, uid, id.orig_h, id.orig_p, id.resp_h, id.resp_p, version, cipher, server_name, resumed, established, cert_chain_fps (fingerprint of the server certificate in x509.log; (empty) for TLS 1.3, which hides the certificate)
column_notes.zeek notice.log: ts, uid, id.orig_h, id.resp_h, id.resp_p, note, msg, src, dst, p, actions
column_notes.zeek http.log: ts, uid, id.orig_h, id.orig_p, id.resp_h, id.resp_p, trans_depth, method, host, uri, referrer, version, user_agent, request_body_len, response_body_len, status_code, status_msg, tags, resp_fuids, resp_mime_types; uid equals the uid of the connection in conn.log
column_notes.zeek files.log: ts, fuid, tx_hosts, rx_hosts, conn_uids, source, depth, analyzers, mime_type, filename, duration, local_orig, is_orig, seen_bytes, total_bytes, missing_bytes, overflow_bytes, timedout, md5, sha1; fuid is listed in http.log resp_fuids
column_notes.zeek x509.log: ts, fingerprint, certificate.version, certificate.serial, certificate.subject, certificate.issuer, certificate.not_valid_before, certificate.not_valid_after, certificate.key_alg, certificate.sig_alg, certificate.key_type, certificate.key_length, certificate.exponent, san.dns, basic_constraints.ca, host_cert, client_cert; one row per certificate per day, at its first sighting
column_notes.mail_gateway verdict / action: clean / delivered for ordinary mail; blocked attachment type / quarantined and sender failed authentication / rejected for the messages behind mail alerts
column_notes.employee_vpn_sessions.csv: One row per session of the employee VPN: the account, the address it connected from and that address's network label, the device (a registry laptop or a home computer named DESKTOP-/LAPTOP-XXXXXXX), the pool address it was given (the DHCP log has the same lease) and the byte counts (the Zeek conn row to the VPN concentrator has the same). A remote-desktop connection from assigned_ip to a workstation appears in conn.log and as a type 10 logon in the Windows Security log.

address_ranges: Internal hosts use 10.14.0.0/16 (corporate), 10.72.0.0/16 (operations) and 172.20.5.0/24 (internet-facing). All external addresses and domain names are invented for the exercise and do not refer to real hosts.
portal_notes: Both logs record every request: people, and the crawlers, monitors and scripts that visit any public site. aid_portal_access: there are no accounts until registration opens at 2027-11-13T06:00Z (midnight local). account_ref is the account a request belongs to (payments/aid_applications.csv account_id; on the logistics system an air-station account of partner_it_registry.json) and is empty when a sign-in name matches no account. client_network is the network of the address as ASN <number>, or base network; the same address carries the same number in every stream. event: page_view, login_success, login_failed, account_created, validation_error, application_submitted, document_uploaded, password_reset_requested, profile_updated: <field>, request_submitted. A month too large for one file is written as _01, _02 in time order.
